message.content:
Here’s a quick‑look calendar of the Canadian federal public holidays that create “long weekends” in 2023.  (If a holiday falls on a weekend, the next weekday is usually observed.)  

| Holiday | Calendar Date (2023) | Observed (if different) | Typical Long‑Weekend Span |
|---------|----------------------|--------------------------|---------------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Sunday Jan 1 | Monday Jan 2 | **Dec 30–Jan 2** (Fri–Mon) |
| Family Day (Ontario, Alberta, Saskatchewan, etc.) | Monday Feb 20 | — | **Feb 18–20** (Sat–Mon) |
| Good Friday | Friday Apr 7 | — | **Apr 7–8** (Fri–Sun) |
| Victoria Day | Monday May 22 | — | **May 20–22** (Sat–Mon) |
| Canada Day | Saturday Jul 1 | Monday Jul 3 | **Jul 1–3** (Sat–Mon) |
| Labour Day | Monday Sep 4 | — | **Sep 2–4** (Sat–Mon) |
| Thanksgiving | Monday Oct 9 | — | **Oct 7–9** (Sat–Mon) |
| Remembrance Day | Saturday Nov 11 | Friday Nov 10 | **Nov 10–12** (Fri–Sun) |
| Christmas Day | Monday Dec 25 | — | **Dec 23–25** (Sat–Mon) |
| Boxing Day | Tuesday Dec 26 | — | (Often counted with Christmas) |

**Quick notes**

* If you’re looking at *observed* dates only, the long weekends above are the ones that actually give you an extra day off.  
* Some provinces have extra holidays (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in NL, Civic Holiday in BC, etc.).  Those would add more long‑weekend opportunities.  
* The “typical long‑weekend span” column shows the full stretch of days that includes the holiday and the adjacent weekend days.  

Feel free to copy/paste this table into your holiday‑planning app!
